title: 9.2 Populations, Samples, and Hypotheses

icans: I can tell the difference between a population and a sample, and between a parameter and a statistic.
I can use a simulation to find proportions.
I can use a simulation to decide whether to reject a hypothesis.

vocab: the entire group you want ______________ about
a claim about a _________________ of a population
a model of a ____________ situation, often using random numbers or coins

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem: A school surveys 100 of its 1,200 students about the lunch menu. Identify the population and the sample.

notes: Parameter or statistic: A parameter describes a _______________; a statistic describes a _______________.

blocks.stem:
Tell whether each number is a parameter or a statistic.
a.  The mean age of all 30 members of a club is 34.
b.  In a survey of 1,000 voters, 52% plan to vote yes.

notes: Testing a hypothesis: Reject a hypothesis when the result is very _______________ if the hypothesis is true.

blocks.stem: You claim a coin is fair. In 50 flips, you get 34 heads. A simulation of 200 trials of 50 fair coin flips gave 34 or more heads in only 2 trials. What should you conclude?

Tell whether each data set is a population or a sample.
a.  the ages of every person counted in a town’s census
b.  the heights of 30 randomly chosen 10th graders

tickets.stem: A sample of 50 of a school’s 800 students is surveyed. What is the population?
Is the mean of a sample a parameter or a statistic?
